inspiration.observed_pattern: Multiple CTEs first aggregate per-customer facts and then filter the aggregate before joining it to customer metadata for a deterministic report.
inspiration.mysql_mariadb_translation: Reauthored as a customer-award archive: grouped purchase totals and counts flow through two CTEs into INSERT ... SELECT, qualifying customers receive a CASE-derived award label, and RETURNING exposes generated archive IDs and aggregate values. The source schema, names, thresholds, and report purpose are new.

fixture_notes: Customers 11 and 13 meet the total-spend threshold and receive archive rows. Customer 12 is below the threshold and remains absent; customer 14 has no purchases and is also absent.
determinism_notes: Fixed customer and purchase IDs, explicit customer ordering before generated archive IDs, fixed numeric thresholds, and ordered final-state checks; no clocks, randomness, sleeps, or concurrent connections are used.
setup: CREATE TABLE customer_directory (customer_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, segment_code VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)
CREATE TABLE purchase_events (purchase_id INT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL, amount INT NOT NULL)

CREATE TABLE spend_awards (award_id INT AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY, customer_id INT NOT NULL, customer_name VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL, total_spent INT NOT NULL, purchase_count INT NOT NULL, award_label VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL)

steps.sql: INSERT INTO spend_awards (customer_id, customer_name, total_spent, purchase_count, award_label) WITH per_customer AS (SELECT customer_id, SUM(amount) AS total_spent, COUNT(*) AS purchase_count FROM purchase_events GROUP BY customer_id), qualifying AS (SELECT customer_id, total_spent, purchase_count FROM per_customer WHERE total_spent >= 50) SELECT q.customer_id, d.customer_name, q.total_spent, q.purchase_count, CASE WHEN q.total_spent >= 80 THEN 'priority' ELSE 'standard' END FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN customer_directory AS d ON d.customer_id = q.customer_id ORDER BY q.customer_id RETURNING award_id, customer_id, customer_name, total_spent, purchase_count, award_label

checks.sql: SELECT award_id, customer_id, customer_name, total_spent, purchase_count, award_label FROM spend_awards ORDER BY award_id
SELECT customer_id, customer_name, segment_code FROM customer_directory ORDER BY customer_id
SELECT purchase_id, customer_id, amount FROM purchase_events ORDER BY purchase_id
